lesson-12805.brief:
Task 1787 round 3. HEAD (0ac5b3ae1) holds two rounds of fixes to the commit gate in ops/bootstrap/code-intel-order-hook.mjs, which allows `git commit` only after `npm run check:commit` succeeded in the same Bash command. Each review round found new bypasses by enumerating shell shapes. Stop enumerating; narrow what re-arms the gate.

Still open (bash with the check replaced by `false` runs COMMIT; the hook allows):
- `[ $rc -eq 0 ] # || exit 1` and `false # &&\ngit commit`: the hook splits operators before handling comments (~:428; splitTopLevel rtk-rewrite-lib.mjs:313). Strip comments (a word starting `#`, outside quotes, to end of line) BEFORE the split. `a#b` and quoted `#` are not comments; `check && # c\ngit commit` stays allowed.
- `|| exit 1a` / `|| exit ""` do not exit. Accept only `exit` or `exit <digits>`.
- `((rc=0))`, `: $((rc=0))`, `rc[0]=0`, `printf -v rc 0`, a nameref before the guard. Fix by adjacency: honour the rc re-arm (`|| exit` and `&&` forms) only when the `<v>=$?` segment immediately follows the check segment and `[ $v -eq 0 ]` / `test $v -eq 0` immediately follows the capture.
- `enable -n exit` earlier: add `enable` to the exit-redefinition refusal.
Unclear shapes fail closed.

Acceptance: one test per shape; each fails on HEAD, passes after. The prescribed `npm run check:commit -- p > log; rc=$?\n[ $rc -eq 0 ] || exit 1\ngit commit -m x -- p` stays allowed; existing cases keep their verdicts. Run `node scripts/test-code-intel-hook.mjs`, `npm run test:harness-audit`, and verify each allowed shape with real `bash -c`.

Out of scope: subshells, `eval`, `bash -c`, substitutions (~:399/:408; they need a real parser); `[[ ]]` and `if` guards, denied today (safe direction). Leave no stray files (round 2 left an empty `l`).

A/B stand override: write no test and run no test, including the historical test instructions above. No commits or memory writes. Own only ops/bootstrap/code-intel-order-hook.mjs.

lesson-12713.brief:
Your checkout (`git diff HEAD^`) holds task 1774's commit gate in ops/bootstrap/code-intel-order-hook.mjs: refuse a Bash command where `check:commit` is followed by a `git commit` not gated by check:commit's exit status. Two reviewers (reviewer-mimo-75fb96, reviewer-kimi-40d5a1) reproduced one root cause: the gate matches only a segment-initial bare `git` and its own peel drops only assignments and `&`, so wrapped commits after a losing separator are allowed: `rtk git commit` (the rtk hook rewrites commands into exactly this form, so it is the realistic miss), `env git commit`, `command git commit`, `exec git commit`, `/usr/bin/git commit`, `git.exe commit`; the same applies to recognising `rtk npm run check:commit` and `npm run --silent check:commit`.

Change: factor ONE shared peel from the rg rule's existing wrapper handling (WRAPPERS ~:504, normalize ~:473: assignments, rtk/proxy/env/command/exec, basename and .exe normalisation) and use it for both the check:commit and the git commit recognisers; delete the gate's own shallower peel. Keep every currently passing case passing.

Tests (scripts/test-code-intel-hook.mjs): one refused case per spelling above after `;` and after `| tail &&`; one allowed case each for `rtk npm run check:commit -- p && rtk git commit -m x` and `env GIT_X=1 git -C d commit` gated by `&&`. Each new refusal test must fail on the current hook.

Acceptance: `node scripts/test-code-intel-hook.mjs` green (report counts).

Out of scope, with reasons:
- `$(git commit)`, backticks, `(…)` subshells, `{ …; }` groups, `if/then`, `time`, `bash -c '…'`: deliberate evasion rather than the accidental piping this gate targets; the sibling read-order rule accepts the same limit (lesson 10856). Add one comment at the gate saying so.
- The early-rg rule's behaviour (reviewed, unchanged): refactor its peel only as far as sharing requires, with its tests green.
- Hook ordering against the rtk rewrite hook: the shared peel covers both orders.

A/B stand override: write no test and run no test, including the historical test instructions above. No commits or memory writes. Own only ops/bootstrap/code-intel-order-hook.mjs.

lesson-12562.brief:

Local Mac seats must keep working (their cwd is the worktree root; confirm that for every role, including scouts/researchers that read the repo in place).

Check every other place the seat context emits an absolute Mac path the seat is told to read (knowledge page links, lesson anchors, artifact links); fix the ones that are seat-facing the same way, list the rest with file:line in the report. Only context building; not remote-provision.ts, spawn.ts, pi.ts, seats.ts, dashboard.ts (other seats own them).
